question: In the pyrolysis of oil shale kerogen, by how many degrees does the maximum of the H2 signal occur earlier under air than under nitrogen?
expect: about 120 C: maximum near 330 C in air vs near 450 C in nitrogen (sec. 3.3.1)
trap: the 50 C earlier onset of mass loss

Roberto C. Chucuya Huallpachoque holds a Master’s degree in
Mechanical Engineering from the Pontifical Catholic University of
Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio, Brazil), with specialization in Thermal
Sciences (2008−2010). He graduated in Energy Engineering from the
Universidad Nacional del Santa (Peru) (2001−2005). He is currently
a faculty member in the Energy Engineering Program at the
Universidad Nacional del Santa (since 2010) and in the Industrial
Engineering Program at the Universidad César Vallejo (since 2012).
His experience is focused on thermofluids and efficient energy use,
particularly in the areas of Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics,
Turbomachinery, and Heat Transfer.

Edwin Santiago Rios Escalante graduated in Mechanical Engineering
from the Universidad Nacional de Trujillo (Peru) in 2014. He
obtained his master’s and doctoral degrees from ″Júlio de Mesquita
Filho″ − UNESP (Brazil) in 2016 and 2021, respectively. He also
worked on two postdoctoral projects (2022 and 2023) at ″Júlio de
Mesquita Filho”. His main areas of interest are biomass conversion
into biofuels, large- and small-scale power generation plants, and
integrated systems for energy generation and biofuel production.
Lately, he has started a deep study of Natural Philosophy to
understand nature’s behavior more rigorously.

7. Alex M. Bimbato

3. Luis Fernando Junior Saldañ a Bernuy

Alex M. Bimbato holds a degree in Mechanical Engineering from the
Federal University of Itajubá (UNIFEI, formerly EFEI), obtained in
2006. He received his Master’s (2008) and Ph.D. (2012) degrees in
Mechanical Engineering, with a focus on Fluid Dynamics and
Turbomachinery, from the same institution. He is currently a
professor at the School of Engineering and Sciences of São Paulo
State University (FEG/UNESP). His work is focused on the field of
Fluid Mechanics, particularly on numerical simulation of flows using
particle methods, computational aerodynamics, vortex shedding
suppression, and ground effect.

Luis Fernando Junior Saldaña Bernuy holds a Master’s degree from
the Graduate Program in Engineering at São Paulo State University
(UNESP, Brazil). He earned his degree in Energy Engineering from
the Universidad Nacional del Santa (Peru) in 2018. He also holds a
diploma in Occupational Health, Safety, and Environmental Management from the Universidad Nacional de Piura (Peru). He has
professional experience in electromechanical engineering, with a focus
on strategic operations management, maintenance planning and
control, and quality management in the industrial fishing, nonmetallic
mining, and railway sectors, with emphasis on energy generation and
control. His academic and research work includes scientific
publications in the field of heat transfer and transport phenomena.
He was awarded a Master’s scholarship by the Brazilian National
Agency of Petroleum, Natural Gas and Biofuels (ANP) through the
PRH 34.1 program at FEG/UNESP.
